**Not without breaking the first release invariant.** The rules file says `is.waiwai.dictation` is permanent because existing Accessibility permission grants depend on it. It's your rule, so you can overrule it, but I'd recommend keeping the identifier.

Renaming would cost every existing install the following:

- **Accessibility grant is lost.** macOS ties the grant to the bundle identifier, so the renamed app counts as a new app. Dictation silently stops working until each user re-grants it in System Settings, and the same applies to Microphone and any other privacy permissions.
- **Preferences reset.** Settings are stored under the bundle identifier, so they disappear unless you write a migration.
- **Other things keyed on the ID may break.** I can't see the repo in this session, so check for Application Support paths, keychain items, login item registration, and the Sparkle update path from old builds to the renamed one.

Users almost never see the bundle identifier. If the goal is for the app to appear as OpenRamble, change the display name (`CFBundleName` / `CFBundleDisplayName`) and the product name, and leave the ID alone. That gets you the branding with none of the breakage.

The one case where renaming is reasonable is if the only existing installs are yours and a few testers who can re-grant permissions by hand. Then before launch is the cheapest time it will ever be. If you go that way, update the invariant in the rules file and `docs/release.md` in the same change.

Do you have existing installs beyond your own machines?
